database: analyst/db/sales.sqlite (SQLite). Query it only through analyst/validate_sql.mjs.
currency_note: Monetary columns are in the order's local currency. Convert to USD with orders.fx_rate_to_usd.

columns.name: text
columns.region: text: AMER | EMEA | APAC (the customer's home region)
columns.is_test_account: integer 0/1. 1 = internal test account; exclude from all business metrics

columns.order_date: text, ISO date the order was placed. Revenue timing uses this column.
columns.currency: text: USD | EUR | JPY (local order currency)
columns.fx_rate_to_usd: real, rate on the order date. Multiply local amounts by this to get USD.

order_items.grain: one row per product line within an order

returns.grain: one row per returned quantity event on an order item

columns.return_date: text, ISO date the return happened. Refund timing uses this column.
columns.refund_amount: real, local currency of the original order

warnings: returns is at order-item level. Reaching it from orders needs order_items; joining orders directly to returns is not possible without that bridge.
orders has many order_items, so summing order-level columns after a join to order_items will overcount.
order_date and return_date are different events and can fall in different fiscal years.
